newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metal futures slip, longs liquidate.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metal futures slip, longs liquidate.

text.p: Yen-denominated Tokyo precious metal futures extended early losses to end lower on Tuesday, pressured by long liquidation when the yen recovered against the dollar in volatile currency trading, traders said.
Gold prices ranged from three yen to 11 yen per gram lower, with benchmark December ending down four yen at 1,326 yen.
"Private investors who held massive longs in gold futures have started to liquidate their positions," one trader said.
The recent slump in the Japanese stock market also prompted investors to liquidate longs, as they use stock shares as collateral for their positions, he said.
Spot gold was quoted at $353.20/50 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $353.30/80 in New York on Monday.

In the bullion market, selling by Australian producers dented prices early, although the market subsequently managed to steady as short covering by funds absorbed arbitrage-related selling from Japan, traders said.
But traders said sentiment toward gold remained bearish.
Weaker physical demand in Asia, a rise in global output, lingering fears of central bank selling and the firm U.S. stock market were all cited as negative factors for gold.
"Initial support is seen at $350," one trader said.
